title: Family Picnic Day Out Checklist: What to Pack
description: The family picnic checklist for days out: food that travels well, keeping it cool, what to bring for kids, and whether attractions allow picnics.
h1: The family picnic day out checklist
intro: A good picnic saves money and stops “hangry” meltdowns. Here’s what to pack for a family day out, and what to check before you bring food into an attraction.

image.alt: A family sitting on a picnic blanket in the grass

keywords: what to pack for a day out
cardText: What to pack, how to keep it cool and which attractions allow picnics.

blocks.title: Scout’s picnic rule
blocks.text: Check the attraction’s food policy before you pack. Most parks, zoos and heritage sites have picnic areas, but some restrict glass, alcohol or cool boxes.
points: Freeze water bottles to use as ice packs

sections.html:
• Wraps and sandwiches that won’t go soggy (pack fillings separately for little ones).
  • Chopped fruit and veg sticks.
  • Cheese, crackers and cold pasta salads.
  • A treat for later, which works brilliantly as a bribe on the way home!

• Cool bag with ice packs or frozen bottles.
  • Picnic blanket with a waterproof backing.
  • Refillable water bottles.
  • Wipes, hand gel, kitchen roll and bin bags.
  • Plates, cups and cutlery (reusable is cheaper over time).
Keep perishable food cool, in the shade, and eat it within a few hours. Throw away anything that’s been sitting in the sun. The UK Food Standards Agency has more food safety guidance.
Most zoos, theme parks and heritage sites have picnic areas, and free days out like beaches and parks are perfect. More saving ideas in days out on a budget.

faqs.q: Can you take a picnic to theme parks?
faqs.a: Many UK theme parks allow picnics and have picnic areas, but rules on cool boxes, glass and alcohol vary. Check the park’s website before you go.
